newsitem.title: UK: UK wool sale sees good competition, better tone.
newsitem.headline: UK wool sale sees good competition, better tone.

text.p: Good competition resulted in a much better tone than seen recently at the 8th sale of the season in Bradford.
The Committee of London Wool Brokers, acting on behalf of the British Wool Marketing Board, offered a total of 2,434,553 million kilos of British Wool.
Bred wools sold well and there was also more interest in Blackface at a lower price to result in a clearance of 88 percent.
Compared with the last Scottish sale on March 26, Cheviots were at par to 2.5 percent dearer and Blackface were fully five percent cheaper.
Against the last Bradford sale on April 30 Halfbreds were fully five percent dearer and Crosses were 2.5 percent dearer.
